paragraphs.text: The people cry to God against the barbarous tyranny of the Babylonians who spoiled God's inheritance, polluted his temple, destroyed his religion, and murdered his people.

paragraphs.text: The prophets show to what extremities God sometimes allows his Church to fall to exercise their faith, before he sets his hand to deliver them.

paragraphs.text: Their friends and relatives did not dare to bury them for fear of the enemies.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: Of which some came from Abraham but were degenerate: and others were open enemies to your religion, but they both laughed at our miseries.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Will you completely consume us for our sins, before you take us to mercy?
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Which we and our fathers have committed.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Seeing we have no other Saviour, neither can we help ourselves, and also by our salvation your Name will be praised: therefore O Lord, help us.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Who though in respect to God they were justly punished for their sins, yet in consideration of their cause were unjustly murdered.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: Who were captives among their enemies and could look for nothing but death.
